title: Startup runway token sandbox
content:
Context:
random back-of-envelope notes for a founder-friendly starter plan and runway math. not intended for final pricing — just quick heuristics to check plausibility for a low-touch PLG onramp. hypotheses, not decisions.

Assumptions (high level):
- target audience: early-stage startups and indie devs (high trial velocity, low $/month initially)
- core metric: net new active projects per week; secondary: conversion to paid in 60d
- product usage: majority short-interaction chat and embeddings (document search) — avg tokens per session ~ 1.8k in first 30s of interaction for dev/test; heavy jobs (fine-tune/long generation) are rare for this cohort.

Key cost levers to convert to approximate per-API-call marginal cost:
1) GPU-hour -> token conversion (amortized)
   - baseline: p4d-like node effective cost to Redwood (reserved/hybrid pricing) = $6 / GPU-hour (optimistic internal econ for committed pools).
   - throughput: assume steady-state throughput of 350k tokens/sec per node (with batching + KV cache for retrieval-heavy). That is 1.26B tokens/hour.
   - pure compute cost per 1k tokens = (6 / 1,260,000) * 1,000 = $0.00476 per 1k tokens.
   - plus infra overhead (network, control plane, model weights memory tax) ~ +35% => ~ $0.0064 per 1k tokens.
   - ops margin, redundancy (SLOs/fallback) add another +50% => retail unit cost target ~ $0.0096 per 1k tokens.
   => ballpark marginal cost 1kT = $0.009–0.012 depending on conservative buffer.

2) Embeddings unit (512-d) cheaper because smaller model and batching: approx 0.4x generation token cost => ~ $0.004 per 1k tokens equivalent. (useful for bucketization)

Startup runway sketch (example cohort economics):
- activation funnel: 10k signups seeded by content/SEO -> 4k active in week 1 -> 400 paying in 60d if conversion 10%
- CAC (organic/low-media) = $8 effective blended (credits+ops)
- target payback < 90d. So LTV must be > CAC * 2 ideally.

Tier ideas (starter play):
1) Free Starter (activation-focused):
   - 10,000 free tokens per account for 30d (credit) + 30k more if verify org/email (spam control).
   - Rationale: low friction but enough to spin up a prototype. 10k tokens ≈ 5 full small conversations or ~1 embedding-heavy flow. Cost to Redwood: ~ $0.00012 (10k tokens * $0.012/1k) => $0.00012? wait math check: 10k tokens = 10 * 1k tokens. At $0.01 per 1k tokens cost => 10 * 0.01 = $0.10. So reserve: free credit cost ~ $0.10 per new user.
   - That means at 10k signups/week cost ~ $1k/week in credit burn. Manageable for early PLG.

2) Hobby (pay-as-you-go):
   - no monthly commitment, $0.02 per 1k tokens retail, embeddings $0.015 per 1k-equivalent.
   - includes burst protection: first 50k tokens/month charged at 50% discount.
   - landing economics: gross margin ~ 40–60% on token revenue depending on realized infra stacking.

3) Startup (commit / monthly):
   - $99/mo for 2M tokens (anchored, encourages light production but capped) => implied $0.0495 per 1k tokens retail. That seems high for 2M pack; re-evaluate: 2M tokens / 1k = 2000 units. $99/2000 = $0.0495 per 1k. That's too high. Better: $99/mo for 10M tokens => $0.0099 per 1k, which is below marginal cost. So change: $99/mo => 2M reserved + 5M at discounted rate. Hmm.
   - Simpler: $99/mo = 2M tokens included, overage $0.008 per 1k (close to cost). This makes included allocation cheap for the user but expensive for Redwood. Need cap. Alternative: $99 gets 2M, overage $0.02/1k. That keeps some uplift revenue.

4) Scale / Team SKU:
   - $1,200/mo = 40M tokens included + 1 seat, $30 per extra seat. Unit price ~ $0.03 per 1k (if fully used). For teams running production, we expect higher efficiency (KV cache, prefix reuse) so unit cost is lower for us. Provide SLA and support.

Notes on included tokens vs pooled/credits:
- included tokens are a great conversion lever but dangerous long term if priced below unit cost. Use usage profiling to gate (eg. free for evaluation flows, not for bulk generation).
- suggest 'starter credits' be time-limited and tied to experiment templates (so we can track conversion from specific product funnels).

Batching / cache sensitivity:
- 'developer test' traffic: low concurrency, many short sessions -> lower batching efficiency -> per-token cost higher (we should inflate effective cost by x1.6 for these flows).
- production retrieval-heavy traffic -> higher cache hit -> effective cost down by x0.6. So pricing should reflect underlying usage patterns: allocate 'cheap' tokens for retrieval/embedding buckets and 'expensive' tokens for small one-off gen.

Activation credit sizing rule of thumb:
- target 1–2 meaningful experiments per signup. Set credit = 100k tokens for seeded startups? that's borderline expensive. Better: 25k tokens per account for verified startups; 10k for general free accounts.
- expected conversion lift per extra 10k tokens ~ +0.5–1% (empirical, noisy).

Quick LTV sample (assume starter cohort):
- cohort of 1,000 signups -> 400 active -> 40 payers (10% conv in 60d)
- average paid ARR for these small users after 6 months ~= $360 (avg $30/mo) => LTV ~ $360
- CAC (credits + activation marketing) = $8 -> payback favorable. But sensitive to churn. If monthly churn 10% leading to mean lifetime 10 months -> LTV higher, ok. If churn 30% -> lifetime ~3 months -> LTV ~ $90 => bad.

Operational constraints (practical rules):
- Cap single free account consumption to 5 requests/min or 150k tokens/day to prevent abuse.
- Ticketing: auto flag accounts >500k tokens in 7d for review (fraud or production use).
- For accounts flagged as production, suggest migration path to reserved capacity or dedicated offering (because those customers should be on Commit).

Experiment ideas (A/B candidates):
- A: 10k free tokens vs B: 30k free tokens for verified org signups; measure 60d paid conversion and time-to-first-paid.
- A: credits tied to 'templates' (search/QA/chat) vs B: generic credits; measure template adoption and retention.
- A: show estimated $ per 1k tokens in console to educate users and reduce support friction vs B: hide pricing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- validate realistic GPU-hour->token throughput with infra (SRE/serving runtime team) — need an updated internal benchmark for conflated model mix (chat+embedding mix). (see JIRA-2315 request)
- what is realistic margin reserve we should hold for free credits? suggest 2–3 months burn caps per marketing budget.
- legal / abuse: confirm KYC thresholds for startup credits.

References / tickets:
- JIRA-1234: starter-credit-ops-constraints
- Confluence: PRICE-ANCHOR-2025 (draft of anchored tier table)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pricing-protos/pull/87 (proto for credits & usage tracking)

Notes to self:
- run a quick Monte Carlo with churn sensitivity (0–30%), conversion 5–15%, avg spend $10–100/mo to see break-evens.
- keep starter-credit per-user cost <= $2 on average for mass acquisition. That suggests free credit <= 200k tokens if unit cost $0.01/1k? Wait: 200k tokens => 200 * $0.01 = $2. So 200k tokens is expensive. Better keep free credit mostly under 25k–50k range.

Rough action items:
- ask infra benchmarks (Ethan) for three realistic cost curves: dev, retrieval-heavy, high-gen.
- spin up small spreadsheet to simulate cohorts and credit burn per acquisition channel. Link to PR above for instrumentation.
- propose two test variants to growth: "microstarter 10k" and "verified 30k" for next quarter.

End.
